Been playing off and on since the original OW1 beta, roughly 1000 hours across multiple platforms. The game had a ton of promise, but Activision-Blizzard have bled the IP of pretty much any creativity and innovation that it once had.

The skins are overpriced, and you can earn most of them for free in lootboxes. Some of the ingame shop bundles cost over $120 USD, sometimes for skins that are just recolors of free skins. The 'Invasion' DLC is a watered down mode that plays similar to the other PvE seasonal events, and is not at all the campaign mode that they had hyped up and been spending dev time on for 5 years. They spent very little dev time on active development and content for those 5 years, so the game stagnated for nothing and now they're struggling to catch back up to the rest of the gaming industry. Stadium mode is listed on the store page still as 'brand new mode', but the mode is no longer getting support- not all characters and maps are playable in this mode. The community is one of the most toxic ones that's still active. Not to mention a heavily overtuned skill-based matchmaking system that all but guarantees that you never win or lose more than 2 games in a row, ever. It can have good moments if you've got a team of friends and everyone's having a good time, but there are other games that do Overwatch's mechanics better, there are games with better communities, there are games where the devs actually add content. Check out Deadlock, Deep Rock Galactic, Helldivers. One of those is free and the others go on sale pretty frequently.

claims.claim: Reviewers report that the competitive matchmaking system places inconsistent or mismatched players together, leading to unbalanced matches.

citations.review_text:
You can have an entire session of bad matchmaking, where you're just facing stacks with each member ranked highly in comp, all using the most toxic characters. You can steamroll the occasional team, wondering how the heck matchmaking put those people together. You get matches where both teams overwhelmingly pick Escort, despite one team having next to no hope of winning without coordination and a 2-2-2 class spread. It can be an absolute ****show and there's no way of predicting it. Then you get hit with a penalty when you try to quit out.

But sometimes you get games where everything is just perfect, where the gap between the teams is small, where each character's unique identity is on full display, and everyone just seems to be enjoying themselves. Yes you have to wade through some absolute dregs to improve, but when you do, more matches will take on a fun complexion, and eventually, you'll be absolutely hooked on the gameplay.

The matchmaking in this game is somehow as bad as—or worse than—Marvel Rivals. I am constantly getting matched with brand-new players who don't understand hero shooters, while the enemy team is stacked with players who are level 100+ on their mains.

The 'just pick to counter' argument falls apart when every game devolves into both sides swapping to the same 5 or 6 busted meta picks. On top of that, roster balance is in a terrible state—tanks have obvious developer favorites while others sit forgotten, and Mei can somehow still stall a point while completely invulnerable in her ice shell, among a myriad of other balance issues that make some characters literal gods and others complete throws.

In a proper hero shooter, every character should have a place. When a broken counter-pick meta forces everyone onto the exact same lineup, the game stops being fun. Putting brand-new players against seasoned all-stars isn't balance; it's broken matchmaking.

claims.claim: Matchmaking places poorly skilled teammates against coordinated opponents.

citations.review_text:
I genuinely don't know how a game can be this good and this annoying at the same time.

Overwatch 2 has some of the best hero designs, abilities, and team fights I've ever experienced in a game. Every match feels different, and there's always something new to learn. Landing a perfect ultimate, saving your entire team at the last second, or winning a fight that looked completely lost is an unreal feeling.

But then you queue ranked, get teammates who look like they've never touched a keyboard before, lose three games in a row, and suddenly you're questioning every decision that led you to download this game.

The balance isn't always great, matchmaking can be questionable, and ranked sometimes feels like a social experiment designed to test patience. Still, I keep coming back because when Overwatch is good, it's REALLY good.

There's no other game quite like it. The movement, the abilities, the team coordination, the clutch moments, the absolute chaos of a team fight — it's all incredibly satisfying.

I hate this game and love it at the same. I'll probably be playing it tomorrow.

10/10 gameplay, 2/10 matchmaking, 0/10 peace of mind. Would recommend.
